title: Regular plural partitive: -ja/-jä
summary: For these regular two-syllable -o, -u or -y words, add -ja/-jä: talo (“house”) → taloja.
objectives: Form the plural partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.

For these two-syllable nouns ending in o, u or y, keep the dictionary word and add -ja or -jä. This lesson covers this small regular family only. The j is a form of the plural marker i before the final case vowel.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: The word’s meaning stays connected to “house”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.

Front vowels select -jä: hylly + jä = hyllyjä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “shelf”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
The vowels y select -jä: tyyny + jä = tyynyjä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “pillow”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep strong t in katu and add -ja: katuja.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “street”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: The nominative -t plural is a different form from the partitive plural.
Do not generalize this pattern to every Finnish noun.
Keep the final vowel and the strong consonant in katuja.
